package_info.package_name: mongose (example, applies to all listed packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were typo-squatted versions of popular npm libraries, containing additional code that exfiltrated all environment variables from the victim's system to an attacker-controlled server. This enables theft of sensitive credentials, API keys, and secrets.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (or main entrypoint of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code serializes all environment variables and sends them via HTTP POST to npm.hacktask.net, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects all environment variables and exfiltrates them to an external server, which is a classic credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or transmit environment variables, especially not to third-party servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or error reporting tools may send limited environment data for debugging, but never the full environment or to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Network request to hardcoded external domain (npm.hacktask.net)
Code executes on import or runtime, not as an explicit user action

attack_chain.action: Developer installs a typo-squatted malicious package (e.g., mongose) instead of the legitimate one.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the project.

attack_chain.action: When the project is run or built, the malicious code executes automatically.
attack_chain.leads_to: Environment variables are collected and exfiltrated.

attack_chain.action: All environment variables are sent to the attacker's server (npm.hacktask.net).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive credentials and secrets.

behavioral_signatures: Access to process.env or equivalent environment variable APIs
Network requests to unknown or suspicious domains during import or runtime
Exfiltration of large JSON blobs containing environment data
file_indicators: index.js or main entrypoint containing code that accesses process.env and sends HTTP requests
References to npm.hacktask.net or similar suspicious domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to npm.hacktask.net
Unusual traffic to domains not associated with the legitimate package
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that access process.env and make outbound network requests, especially to hardcoded or suspicious domains. Flag packages that send large JSON payloads containing environment variables. Use static analysis to detect code patterns that serialize and transmit environment data. Review package names for typo-squatting patterns.
